newsitem.title: USA: Exxon, BP have "significant" offshore find.
newsitem.headline: Exxon, BP have "significant" offshore find.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Monday it has a significant Gulf of Mexico deepwater discovery called Hoover.

The well, located about 165 miles south of Galveston, Texas encountered over 100 feet of net hydrocarbon pay. The discovery may contain developable reserves in excess of 100 million barrels of oil equivalent, the company said.
The Hoover field is only 15 miles from Exxon's previously announced Diana discovery, also estimated to be in excess of 100 million barrels, Exxon said.
Exxon is the operator of both, with a 66.7 percent working interest. British Petroleum Co Plc owns the rest.

A project team is evaluating options for the development of Diana and Hoover, Exxon said. Options under review include process facilities installed on a floating structure, which would establish a world water depth record for a floating offshore production structure.
Production start-up would be targeted for the year 2000.

Exxon said Hoover, which encompasses Alaminos Canyon Blocks 25 and 26, was drilled in a water depth of 4,795 feet, using a moored semi-submersible drilling rig. It is located within the same basin as the 1990 Diana discovery on East Breaks Blocks 945 and 946.

The most recent Diana appraisal well established a water depth record for testing from a moored vessel -- 4,657 feet, Exxon said. That appraisal well recorded maximum flows of 4,800 barrels of oil and 2.6 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.

In addition to interests in Alaminos Canyon Blocks 25 and 26, Exxon and BP, either alone or together, have 33 additional blocks under lease in the vicinity of the Hoover and Diana discoveries, Exxon said.
